goal: Turn the observed denominator failure — an evidence summary that counted a missing outcome as zero — into one executable check that reports unrecorded outcome observations separately from recorded zeros, keeps the denominator it actually summarized, and states both the original and the deduplicated counts, so that a summary can no longer be read as if every observation carried a value.

methodTuple.method: Denominator-integrity audit of an aggregated outcome table: classify each observation as recorded value, recorded zero or unrecorded; count the unrecorded ones into an explicit unknown bucket instead of a value; carry the denominator of the observation set actually summarized; recompute the counts after duplicate observations are removed; and report the original and deduplicated counts side by side.
methodTuple.software: none on file: the procedure exists as prose rules in a local teaching set (record unknown separately and keep denominators explicit; detect duplicates before summarizing) and has no executable implementation in this workspace
methodTuple.data: One frozen local teaching table with six observations, five recorded outcomes and one unrecorded outcome, recorded only as the statement 'denominator6, known outcomes5, one missing'; the table itself was not supplied to this run and is not fabricated here
methodTuple.codeArchive: none supplied; no repository, package or script was provided with the teaching input
methodTuple.reportedExamples: one reported example, local and non-published: denominator 6, known outcomes 5, one missing. No published numerical example was retrieved.

developmentCases.situation: Counting failure: an unrecorded outcome value entered the summary as a zero, so the summary states a value where none was observed.
developmentCases.expectedBehaviour: Classify the observation as unrecorded and report it as an unknown count, never as zero, before any aggregate is written.

developmentCases.situation: Boundary case on the repaired output: six observations, five known outcomes, one unrecorded; known plus unrecorded must equal the denominator.
developmentCases.expectedBehaviour: Report denominator 6, known 5, unknown 1, and fail the check when known plus unknown does not equal the denominator or when unknown is reported as 0.

developmentCases.situation: Competing rule: dropping the unrecorded observation while keeping the original denominator, so the denominator no longer describes the summarized set.
developmentCases.expectedBehaviour: Flag the summary because the drop is not stated and the denominator and the summarized set disagree; the audit reports the discrepancy rather than choosing a rule.
